# Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA)

> Cross-cutting: grid core + plugins + `libs/themes` + `apps/docs`. Created after the #45x docs
> a11y sweep because no existing knowledge file had room and the facts span every layer.
> For _how to run_ the scans, see the `run-e2e` and `debug-browser` skills.

## Ownership

OWNS (grid): `A11yMessages` (`core/types.ts` + `core/defaults.ts`), `announce()`
(`core/internal/aria.ts` → `.tbw-sr-only[aria-live=polite][aria-atomic]`), the ARIA role tree in
`core/internal/dom-builder.ts`, `--tbw-color-*` contrast in `core/styles/variables.css`.
OWNS (docs): `apps/docs/src/styles/custom.css` token overrides,
`apps/docs/src/plugins/rehype-aside-role.mjs`, `apps/docs-e2e/tests/a11y.spec.ts`.

## The role tree — what may own what

```
.tbw-grid-root
  .tbw-scroll-area
    .rows-body-wrapper
      .rows-body[role=grid]            ← owns ONLY row / rowgroup
        .header[role=rowgroup] > .header-row[role=row] > .cell[role=columnheader]
        .rows-container[role=presentation]   ← TRANSPARENT: its children are
          .rows-viewport[role=presentation]     promoted into role=grid
            .rows > .data-grid-row[role=row] > .cell[role=gridcell]
  .faux-vscroll
  .tbw-sr-only[aria-live=polite]       ← OUTSIDE role=grid (this is why it works)
```

INVARIANT: because `.rows-container` / `.rows-viewport` are `role="presentation"`, **anything a
plugin mounts under them becomes a direct owned child of `role="grid"`**. Only `row`/`rowgroup`
are legal there. This is the single most common way a plugin breaks `aria-required-children`.

INVARIANT: `role="row"` may only own cell-ish children. A plugin that _replaces_ a row's children
(Responsive card layout) or _adds_ a sibling header row (GroupingColumns) must assign roles itself.

DECIDED (a11y sweep): the empty-state overlay is `role="presentation"`, **not** `role="status"`.
It mounts inside `.rows-container` for `emptyOverlay: 'rows'` and would be promoted into
`role="grid"`. `updateEmptyOverlay()` now takes the host and routes the message through
`announce()` instead — the live region is outside the grid role and is honoured more reliably.
The loading overlay keeps `role="status"` because it mounts on `.tbw-grid-root`.

FLOW (empty state): `#updateEmptyOverlay()` → `updateEmptyOverlay(gridRoot, …, this)` →
`createEmptyOverlay()` (presentational div) → `showEmptyOverlay()` → `announce(host, textContent)`.

DECIDED: Responsive card rows get `role="gridcell"` + `aria-colindex="1"` on the card
(`renderRow`, only when the card has no role) — one spanning cell per row.
DECIDED: GroupingColumns group cells get `role="columnheader"`; **implicit spacer** groups get
`role="presentation"` (`buildGroupHeaderRow`). Note `buildGroupHeaderRow` does not synthesise
implicit groups — `computeColumnGroups` does; tests must pass the synthetic group explicitly.
TENSION: group cells now match bare `[role="columnheader"]` and precede the real header row in DOM
order, so any `.first()` e2e locator silently resolves to a group cell (bare `textContent`, no
`<span>`, no sort/filter affordance) → `locator('span').click()` hangs. e2e selectors must qualify:
`SELECTORS.headerCell` excludes `.header-group-cell`; ad-hoc locators use `[role="columnheader"][data-field]`.

## Naming controls

DECIDED (#45x): Selection checkbox column is named through `A11yMessages`, not hardcoded English —
`selectAllRows()` and `selectRow(rowIndex)` (zero-based), both `@since 3.7.0`. Header uses a
`.tbw-sr-only` span inside the wrapping `<label class="tbw-checkbox-header">`; rows use
`aria-label` on the input. `.tbw-sr-only` lives in `core/styles/base.css`.

TENSION: `A11yMessages` now mixes _announcements_ (live-region text) with _accessible names_
(`selectAllRows` / `selectRow`). Documented as a `:::note` in `guides/i18n.mdx`; do not add more
name-style keys without revisiting the split.

INVARIANT: a **disabled** control still needs an accessible name. `<input type="checkbox" disabled>`
in a custom renderer is announced as a bare "checkbox" — the docs samples in `grid/core.mdx` all
carry `aria-label` for this reason.

DECIDED (#472): `columnheader` cells declare `aria-label = col.header ?? col.field` — **default
plain-text branch only** in `core/internal/header.ts`. `columnheader` takes its name from content,
and "content" includes descendant text alternatives, so the resize handle
(`role="button"` + `aria-label="Width of column X"`, deliberately exposed for SC 2.5.7 and
therefore **not** `aria-hidden`-able) plus the plugin-injected filter button were concatenated into
every header: `"ID ⇅ Width of column ID"`. An explicit label stops the traversal, and is safe
against SC 2.5.3 because it is character-for-character the visible text. A consumer
`headerRenderer` / `__headerTemplate` owns its own naming and is left alone.

DECIDED (#472): the sort indicator is `aria-hidden="true"`. Its glyph is drawn with a CSS
`::before`, which Chrome folds into name-from-content. Nothing is lost — `aria-sort` is maintained
independently in `header.ts` (×2), `sorting.ts`, and `base-plugin.ts`.

## Colour tokens — surface vs text

INVARIANT: a token tuned for **borders/rings/fills** (3:1) is not safe as a **text** colour (4.5:1).
Both design systems in play encode this split:

| System    | Surface token        | Text token                |
| --------- | -------------------- | ------------------------- |
| Starlight | `--sl-color-accent`  | `--sl-color-text-accent`  |
| Grid      | `--tbw-color-accent` | `--tbw-color-accent-text` |

DECIDED: `--tbw-color-accent-text: light-dark(#1d4ed8, #93c5fd)` added to `variables.css`
(+ registry entry in `apps/docs/src/data/css-variable-registry.ts`, + a `:::caution` in the
theming guide). `--tbw-color-accent` stays vivid.

INVARIANT: a theme that overrides `--tbw-color-accent` MUST also define `--tbw-color-accent-text`,
or accent **text** silently keeps the core blue while accent **surfaces** take the theme hue (worst
case: vibrant/material purple accent + blue accent text). All six `libs/themes/dg-theme-*.css`
define it. `bootstrap` needs a distinct value (`#0d6efd` is exactly 4.50:1 on white → `#0a58ca`);
`contrast`, `large`, `material` pin text = surface because their accent already clears 4.5:1.

DECIDED: status palette re-tuned so both stops clear 4.5:1 as **text** (they are used as text by
context-menu danger items and cell renderers): success `hsl(122 39% 34%)` / `hsl(122 39% 49%)`,
error `hsl(0 65% 51%)` / `hsl(0 65% 65%)`. `libs/themes/dg-theme-{standard,vibrant}.css` moved
success to `#047857` (emerald-700); `#059669` is only 3.77:1 on white. `bootstrap` / `material`
themes deliberately untouched — they pass and mirror upstream design systems.

DECIDED (#472, revised): **every** shipped theme is contrast-gated by
`apps/docs-e2e/tests/theme-contrast.spec.ts` — `contrast`/`large` at AAA (7:1),
`standard`/`vibrant`/`bootstrap`/`material` at AA (4.5:1); non-text pairs at 3:1 everywhere.
Supersedes the earlier "aesthetic themes stay ungated" call: the audit showed only 4 pairs actually
failed and **no accent hue had to move**. All three accent failures were white text on a _light_
dark-mode accent, fixed by giving `--tbw-color-accent-fg` a `light-dark()` dark branch (standard
`#0b1220`, vibrant `#1e1b4b`, bootstrap `#052c65`) — the pattern `material` already used, and what
Bootstrap/Material 3 do upstream. Also nudged bootstrap `fg-muted` light `#6c757d`→`#6a737b` (4.45
was 0.05 short) and `border-strong` in standard/vibrant/bootstrap (it bounds the cell editor's
input via `--tbw-border-input`, so it owes SC 1.4.11's 3:1 — not decorative).

INVARIANT: contrast measurement MUST composite alpha. `--tbw-color-row-{alt,hover}` and
`--tbw-color-selection` are translucent (`rgba(0,0,0,0.05)`-style) in `bootstrap`/`material`;
reading `getComputedStyle().backgroundColor` and dropping the alpha scores a 5% black tint as pure
black and fabricates 4 failures. `measure()` in `theme-contrast.spec.ts` composites each background
over `--tbw-color-bg`, then the foreground over that.

DECIDED (#472): `ThemeBuilder.astro`'s contrast panel must agree with the e2e gate, so its maths
lives in `apps/docs/src/data/contrast.ts` (unit-tested by `contrast.spec.ts`) and mirrors
`measure()`. Three real defects fixed: (1) translucent backgrounds were composited over
`--tbw-color-panel-bg` instead of `--tbw-color-bg` (off by up to 1.4 on bootstrap/material row
tints); (2) foreground alpha was dropped — `resolveColor()` round-tripped through hex; (3) the pair
list was 6 of the gate's 11, omitting both non-text pairs, so `border-strong` failures were
invisible. Non-text pairs now grade at 3:1, not the text bars. Verified in-browser: builder ==
ground truth on all 6 themes x 2 modes x 11 pairs. The earlier "suspect it doesn't set
`color-scheme`" hypothesis was **wrong** — `readComputedVariables()` always set it.
Note: `readComputedVariables()` substitutes a concrete colour for tokens that compute
`transparent`; that substitute is now `--tbw-color-bg` (was hard-coded white/`#222`), because a
transparent token shows whatever it sits on.

TENSION: the **base tokens** in `libs/grid/src/lib/core/styles/variables.css` are not gated by
anything — `theme-contrast.spec.ts` always loads one of the 6 theme files. With no theme the
builder flags two real failures: light `accent-fg` `#ffffff` on `accent` `#3b82f6` = **3.68**
(fails AA 1.4.3), and dark `border-strong` `#666666` on the dark grid bg = **2.8** (fails
SC 1.4.11). Same class as the theme fixes above; not yet fixed because it moves default visuals.

INVARIANT: Starlight `--sl-color-gray-3` on `--sl-color-gray-6` is **exactly 4.48:1** in dark mode
— a systematic near-miss. `gray-2` is the safe muted-text token. Nested inside a callout the same
token drops to ~4.0:1, so `starlight-tabs [role=tab]:not([aria-selected=true])` is forced to
`gray-1` in `custom.css`.

INVARIANT: **`opacity` dimming silently breaks 1.4.3.** It fades text as well as chrome and
compounds with any tinted descendant. `.row-inactive { opacity: 0.5 }` measured 3.15:1, and even
0.85 left tinted status cells under 4.5:1. Two remedies: expose the value as a token and pick a
safe stop (`--tbw-selection-disabled-opacity: 0.65` — 0.6 gave 4.24:1, 0.65 gives 5.02:1), or dim
with a **surface tint** instead (what the `RowCellStylingDemo` teaches now).

INVARIANT: one hue cannot clear 4.5:1 on both a pale and a dark tint of itself — tinted
success/warning/danger cells need `light-dark()` foregrounds.

## Landmarks

DECIDED: `apps/docs/src/plugins/rehype-aside-role.mjs` sets `role="note"` on every
`<aside class="starlight-aside">`. `<aside>` is an implicit `complementary` landmark and 16 docs
pages carry 2+ untitled asides (`api-reference.mdx` has 8), so `landmark-unique` fired site-wide —
including on generated TypeDoc pages, which a per-page fix cannot reach. Wired via
`markdown.rehypePlugins` in `astro.config.mjs` (Astro warns this key is deprecated; pre-existing).

## Target size (SC 2.5.8)

TENSION: axe's `target-size` cannot distinguish **scroll clipping from occlusion** — the
half-visible last virtualized row reports as "partially obscured" (an 80×33 cell measured as
80×13). It is therefore disabled in `apps/docs-e2e/tests/a11y.spec.ts` and replaced by an explicit
measurement test.

INVARIANT: that hand-rolled test must honour two SC exceptions or it produces false failures:

1. **Effective target** — a 13×13 native checkbox wrapped in a `<label>` is hit via the label box.
2. **Spacing** — an undersized target passes when a 24px-diameter circle centred on it intersects
   no other target. This is what keeps the grid's 9×31 `.resize-handle` conformant.

DECIDED: the blanket `.rows-viewport` exclusion is gone; the clip is tested explicitly
(`clippedByScroller` — is the box outside the scroller's own rect?). Waving the whole viewport
through hid every in-cell control (tree disclosures, master-detail toggles, row checkboxes,
inline editors) from the measurement.

DECIDED: occluded targets are dropped before the spacing check (`document.elementFromPoint` at the
box centre must resolve to the element, an ancestor, or a descendant). An overlay tool panel sits
_over_ the grid, so its controls land within 12px of row checkboxes nobody can click — which broke
the spacing exception for unreachable targets.

INVARIANT: **settle CSS animations before measuring anything.** Playwright's `visible` is true from
frame 1, so `getBoundingClientRect()` samples mid-animation. `@keyframes tbw-filter-panel-enter`
scales `scaleY(0.3) → 1` over 150ms, and the filter panel's 28px rows measured **12px** — a
fabricated SC 2.5.8 failure. `settleAnimations()` awaits `document.getAnimations()` finished
promises, filtering `iterations === Infinity` (spinners never finish).

Fixed sizes in the docs chrome: `.demo-source-toggle` `min-height: 24px` (was 23.5), DemoControls
`input[type=range]`/`select[data-ctrl]`/radio+check `label` `min-height: 24px`, `.dc-toggle`
24px tall with the 18px track centred (`inset: 3px 0`).

## Test gates

TENSION: `e2e/tests/accessibility.spec.ts` scopes to `tbw-grid`. It no longer blanket-disables
anything: `scrollable-region-focusable` and `aria-required-children` were suppressions that hid
real defects until a manual audit found them, and removing them left the suite green (27/28 — the
angular scan needs port 4200 free). Any exclusion is now argued per test, at the call site.
`apps/docs-e2e/tests/a11y.spec.ts` is the unscoped counterpart: whole-document scan, 10 resting
routes plus 9 transient surfaces, only `color-contrast` and `target-size` disabled.

INVARIANT: a resting-page scan cannot see a surface that does not exist yet. Filter panels, context
menus and submenus, overlay editors, export dialogs, expanded detail/tree rows and the open shell
tool panel are all scanned **after** the interaction that creates them (the `TRANSIENT` table).
Scanning `ShellMultiPanelsDemo` at rest passed while an unlabelled `<select>` sat inside the closed
accordion.

DECIDED: manual verification is done against a **built** site, not the dev server — the port-4400
dev server returns a bare error page here. This is now automated as `tools/docs-a11y-audit.ts`
(`node --experimental-strip-types tools/docs-a11y-audit.ts`): serves `dist/docs` on 4401 from
`node:http`, drives it with Playwright chromium, injects the **local**
`node_modules/axe-core/axe.min.js` (no CDN), and scans 19 curated routes — prose,
TypeDoc-generated reference, splash, 404 — in `light` and `dark`. First clean run: **0 issues**.
`--all` widens to every built route (702), `--json` emits machine-readable findings. Always
aggregate the violations before returning them — a raw `results.violations` payload blows the
context budget. Docs-e2e cannot host this: `apps/docs-e2e/astro.config.mjs` is a **bare harness**
(vite aliases only, no Starlight, no MDX) that serves `/demo/<slug>` and nothing else.

INVARIANT: a `bun tools/*.ts` script may **not** call `chromium.launch()`. Playwright drives the
browser over `--remote-debugging-pipe`; under Bun on Windows the child spawns (`<launched> pid=…`)
but never becomes controllable, so the call hangs for the full 180s timeout. The Playwright _test
runner_ is immune because it spawns its own node worker — `bun nx e2e docs-e2e` is fine. Run
browser-driving tools with `node --experimental-strip-types`; `docs-a11y-audit.ts` guards on
`'Bun' in globalThis` so the failure is a one-second message, not a three-minute stall.

INVARIANT: axe checks _rules_; it does not check that the tree still **says what we mean**.
`apps/docs-e2e/tests/aria-snapshot.spec.ts` pins the accessibility tree with
`toMatchAriaSnapshot({ name: '<x>.aria.yml' })`. The baselines under
`aria-snapshot.spec.ts-snapshots/` **must be committed** — they are the assertion, and a gitignored
baseline is regenerated on first run so every assertion passes vacuously. (Contrast `e2e/snapshots/`,
ignored because visual PNGs are byte-fragile across machines.) Scope each snapshot to the chrome
under test: the first `shell-chrome` baseline swallowed 20 rows of churning demo data.

TENSION: two ARIA-tree defects are known and **not** fixed, pending a decision. (1) Tree rows carry
the `▶`/`▼` glyph in the accessible name and expose no disclosure button — only `aria-expanded` on
the row, unlike master-detail's `button "Expand details"`. This may be the correct treegrid pattern.
(2) `.tbw-filter-panel` has no container role or accessible name, and each option's label text is
announced twice (`checkbox "Alice Johnson"` then `text: Alice Johnson`).

INVARIANT: an axe rule id is **not** proof of a WCAG failure — check `tags` in
`node_modules/axe-core/axe.js` first. `empty-table-header` is `best-practice` / `minor` (not in
`WCAG22AA_TAGS`), and its only check is `has-visible-text`, which `.tbw-sr-only` does **not**
satisfy. sr-only text fixes the accessible _name_ (4.1.2), never a visible-text rule. Rejected
PR #472's ask to name the single-select checkbox header on those grounds — the cell holds no
control there, same as any `header: ''` utility column.
